text:
sam: Hey all — seeing BERTScore drop ~0.03 when we run quantized-int8 runner vs fp16 on the new 7B model. Started a smoke run on the eval harness.

maria: Which dataset + metric config? pass@k or gen metrics?

sam: It's the conversational SQuAD-style eval (gen). BERTScore macro avg. same seed.

kevin: Any difference in tokenization or detokenization steps? quant path sometimes uses fast tokenizer variant.

sam: Good call. I diffed the runner logs: quant runner uses tokenizer=v2 in the container image, fp16 used tokenizer=v1. But we pin tokenizer in config.json right?

jess: Can you paste the runner config you used?

sam: Sure:
```
model: redwood/7b-lr-small
precision: int8
tokenizer: v2
batch: 8
metrics:
  - bert_score: {lang: en, idf: false}
  - exact_match: {}
```

maria: If tokenization differs that can affect BERTScore (subword boundaries). Also check postprocessing trimming and answer alignment.

kevin: Also check bert_score implementation: our eval harness had a change to use sentencepiece-normalized inputs for idf=False mode in PR #4021.

sam: Oh hmm. I ran with the latest eval-runner image which includes #4021. Maybe fp16 runs were older. Re-running fp16 with same runner image.

eval-bot: Triggered job 9234: eval/harness/9234 started (sam) — https://ci.example/9234 :construction:

sam: Re-run results: fp16 now matches previous numbers. Quant int8 still -0.028 on bert_score.

jess: Can you dump tokenization diffs for one failure example? small snippet.

sam: Example input + token lists attached:
sam: INPUT: "Who wrote 'The Raven'?"
sam: fp16 tokens: [Who, wrote, 'The, Raven, ?]
sam: int8 tokens: [Who, wrote, 'The, Rav, en, ?]

maria: there we go — subword split on "Raven" changes BERTScore anchor tokens. That can easily explain 0.02-0.03 drift.

kevin: Two follow-ups: 1) ensure tokenizer pinning across runners; 2) add a small normalization step in metric implementation to join contiguous wordpieces before embedding compute for BERTScore (or use original text-based BERTScore variant).

jess: Filing a short ticket to make tokenization deterministic in harness and add a unit test. @kevin can you own the metric normalization change?

kevin: Yep, will pick up. I'll also add a CI check that runs a tiny tokenization parity test across runner images.

sam: Thanks. For immediate mitigation, I'll add note to model onboarding checklist: explicitly pin tokenizer version and include tokenization samples.

maria: :thumbsup: good plan.

sam: Closing loop — will update this thread when CI PR lands.
